What we know so far:
- Spike started ~07:30 PST; Grafana screenshot attached by customer.
- Initial logs (prelim): elevated 429s from org_id=msync-org / project_id=msync-ingest.
- No scheduled infra maintenance in that window.

Suspected vector: org/project was assigned to a lower quota tier during a background tiering job; rate-limiter evaluated on effective tier and started throttling. This matches other recent tiering boundary regressions.

Immediate asks (high priority):
1) Marcus — can you confirm whether any tiering reassignments ran between 06:30–08:00 PST and provide the diff (quota assignments)? If a bad assignment exists, can we push a temporary override to restore previous quota for msync-ingest?
2) Priyom — if we do a temporary quota lift, please also adjust soft limits / retry-window to avoid immediate retry storms (short-term backoff).
3) Sean — prepare an exec-friendly summary and a customer apology call slot (we may want to do a 1PM PT call).

Please mark this P0. I will coordinate comms and credits if needed.

Quick update:
- I ran the tiering audit. There was an automated reassignment job that ran at 06:45 PST. It incorrectly applied the "standard-saas" tier to project msync-ingest due to a metadata normalization bug (null region tag caused fallback to default tier with lower unit allowance).
- I've staged a hotfix (quota-diff.patch) to revert msync-ingest back to the previous "enterprise-prem" assignment; proposed temporary override applied (effective now) to increase allowed RPS and burst windows.
- Also increasing token-per-second limit for msync-ingest by 3x as a stopgap. We will roll a proper fix to the tiering logic (metadata normalization) in the next deploy (ETA 48h).

Short-term mitigation steps I executed:
- Applied override to org_id=msync-org / project_id=msync-ingest (effective 09:00 PST).
- Bumped soft retry window to 2s and tightened client guidance to jittered exponential backoff.
- Monitor scope: I put an alert on 429 rate and per-project throttle counts.

Initial results: customer-side 429 rate dropped from 28% -> 4% in the first 20m (preliminary). I'll keep monitoring and push full patch for normalization logic tonight.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
